sentences.text: Nyctosaurus, which translates to "night lizard," was a member of the nyctosaurid pterosaur family that inhabited the Late Cretaceous era.
One species featured an exceptionally large, antler-like crest on its skull, a feature preserved in two specimens described in 2003.
Its anatomy closely resembled that of the contemporary genus Pteranodon.
The animal possessed relatively long wings with a shape similar to modern seabirds, particularly the albatross.
The tips of its jaws were thin and needle-sharp.
Unlike other pterodactyloids, which typically had four phalanges in their wing fingers, Nyctosaurus had only three.
This creature grew from hatching to an adult wingspan of over 2 meters in less than a year.
The massive head crest did not begin to develop until the animal reached one year of age.
Calculations estimate its cruising speed at 9.6 meters per second, or 34.5 kilometers per hour.
The genus was first described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1876 based on fragmentary material from the Smoky Hill River site in Kansas.
Marsh named the new genus Nyctosaurus, deriving the name from Greek words for "night" and "lizard."
Marsh later incorrectly changed the genus name to Nyctodactylus in 1881, a name that remains its modern synonym.
Researchers suggest Nyctosaurus flew like modern albatrosses, covering long distances while rarely flapping its wings, and likely spent almost all its time in the air due to impaired ground movement.
Fully adult, large-crested specimens may have lived to be 5 or 10 years old.
Paleontologist Christopher Bennett concluded that the crest was likely used solely for display, though other scientists had hypothesized it supported a flight headsail.
Bennett also argued that the crest was not a sexual dimorphism trait, suggesting both sexes had crests that differed in shape and size.
N. gracilis and N. lamegoi were placed within the family Nyctosauridae as sister taxa to Muzquizopteryx.
According to Andres and Myers (2013), Nyctosaurus is phylogenetically situated within the group Pteranodontia and belongs to the parent group Pterodactyloidea.
During the time Nyctosaurus lived, the region was covered by an extensive shallow sea, and all known fossils come from the Smoky Hill Chalk of Kansas, part of the Niobrara Formation.
Nyctosaurus fossils were deposited in the Smoky Hill Limestone between 85 and 84.5 million years ago during a marine regression of the Niobrara Sea.
The Paleobiology Database lists the time range for Nyctosaurus as the Albian to Maastrichtian stages, spanning from 110.1 to 66 million years ago.
